issues.title: feat: Add "Action Supported By" lookup field to Item Action Description section
issues.description:
## Background

The existing `Program Supported By` field (`ItemActionDescriptionSection.ProgramSupportedByAction`) has a hidden dependency on the PM/PD dropdown via JavaScript and a parent-child `LookupItem.parentId` linking mechanism. This makes it unsuitable for organizations (e.g., JPO Meridian) that need a standalone "supported by" concept not tied to PM/PD selection.

A new independent lookup field — **Action Supported By** — is required. It follows the same implementation pattern as other standard lookup dropdown fields in the form and has no dependency on any other field.

## Scope

Add a new `ActionSupportedBy` lookup dropdown field to the Item Action Description section. The field must be manageable through the existing admin lookup configuration screens and configurable per-organization via `System_FieldMetadata` (hidden, required, conditionally required, etc.).

## Acceptance Criteria

### Database / Migration

*  A new `Lookup` record is created for `ActionSupportedBy` and a corresponding entry is added to the `eLookups` enum in code
  * [ ]  A new column `ActionSupportedBy` (nullable `int`, FK to `LookupItem`) is added to the item table (matching the nullability pattern of `ProgramSupportedByAction`)
  * [ ]  `System_FieldMetadata` seed records are added for each organization that uses this field, matching the same column set as other lookup fields (DisplayName, IsHidden, IsRequired, ConditionallyRequired, IsDuplicate, IsFiltered, AllowDateNA)
  * [ ]  A SQL migration script is included under `Source/Migrations/`

### Admin

*  Lookup items for `ActionSupportedBy` are manageable via the existing Admin \> Lookup Item screens
  * [ ]  The field appears in Admin \> Field configuration for participating organizations, allowing per-org control of visibility, required status, display order, and display name
  * [ ]  No custom admin UI is required beyond what already exists for other lookup fields

### Model / Service / Controller

*  A property `ActionSupportedBy` (nullable `int`) is added to `ItemActionDescriptionSection` (or the relevant view model), consistent with `ProgramSupportedByAction`
  * [ ]  The property is mapped to the new database column via EF or the existing data access pattern
  * [ ]  `PopulateAllLookups` in `ItemController` populates `ViewData["ActionSupportedByDropDownList"]` using `_sprocService.GetLookupItemsFor((int)eLookups.ActionSupportedBy, organizationId)` — no filtering or parent-child lookup
  * [ ]  The field is included in item Create, Edit, and read-only/display paths
  * [ ]  The field value is saved and retrieved correctly on POST

### View / Layout

*  The `ActionSupportedBy` dropdown is added to `_ItemActionDescriptionSection.cshtml` in the same row as `ProgramSupportedByAction`
  * [ ]  Both fields use `BeginHalfSectionFor` so they render side by side when both are visible
  * [ ]  When `ProgramSupportedByAction` is hidden (via `System_FieldMetadata.IsHidden`), `ActionSupportedBy` renders in its place without layout breakage
  * [ ]  When both are visible, they display side by side on a single row, consistent with the existing half-section pairs (e.g., `ServiceOrSupply` / `ItPurchase`)
  * [ ]  `CustomDropDownListFor` is used with the `ViewData["ActionSupportedByDropDownList"]` key, consistent with all other lookup dropdowns
  * [ ]  The field respects the `DisplaySectionAsReadOnly` flag on the section

### No Dynamic Linking

*  The `ActionSupportedBy` dropdown is **not** wired to any `onchange` event on PM/PD or any other field
  * [ ]  No AJAX endpoint (`UpdateSupportedByDDL` or similar) is created or modified for this field
  * [ ]  The dropdown is always populated from the full org-scoped lookup list at page load — no client-side filtering

### General

*  The implementation follows the same end-to-end pattern as other standard lookup fields in the form (e.g., `ServiceOrSupply`, `LevelOfEffort`, `TypeOfAction`)
  * [ ]  No existing `ProgramSupportedByAction` behavior is modified
  * [ ]  Field label text defaults to "Action Supported By" but is overridable per-org via `System_FieldMetadata.DisplayName`

issues.title: refactor: Replace PO/JPO acronyms with Central in all user-visible display text
issues.description:
## Description

The organization is rebranding from "PO" (Program Executive Office) and "JPO" (Joint Program Executive Office) to "Central". This ticket updates all text rendered to the end user in the browser to reflect the new naming. Backend identifiers, database schema, stored procedures, API contracts, C# property/class/method names, and test identifiers are **out of scope** and remain unchanged.

**Replacement rules applied:**

* `PO` → `Central` (all-caps contexts)
* `JPO` → `Central` (all-caps contexts)
* `Peo` → `Cpe` (title-case contexts)

**Organization display name mappings (UI text only):**

| Old | New |
|-----|-----|
| PO Vantage North | Central Riverside |
| PO Data & Analytics | Central Crestline |
| JPO Meridian | Central Meridian |

---

* `Models/PostAwardFollowOnActionViewModel.cs` — "Peo Control Number Follow-on Action"

* `Data/StoredProcedures/Models/GetOneNListItemsByUser.cs` — "PO Control#" (drives column header via `DisplayNameFor`)

**Dropdown display text (`SelectListItem.Text` only — `Value` properties unchanged):**

* `Models/CustomerAccessRequestFormViewModel.cs` — org dropdown options: "JPO Meridian"→"Central Meridian", "PO Vantage North"→"Central Riverside", "PO Data & Analytics"→"Central Crestline"

**CSS navbar brand titles:**

## Acceptance Criteria

*  Navigating to `/Item/Edit` shows tab labeled **"Central Administration"** (not "PO Administration")
  * [ ]  The Central Administration tab shows all field labels using **"Central"** (e.g., "Central Priority Level Override", "Central Adjudication", "Compliance Central Approval")
  * [ ]  The List view column header reads **"Central Control#"** (not "PO Control#")
  * [ ]  The Reports page label reads **"Central Reports"**
  * [ ]  The navbar brand/title reads the correct Central org name for each organization (Central Riverside, Central Crestline, Central Meridian)
  * [ ]  The org selection buttons on the landing page read **Central Riverside**, **Central Crestline**, **Central Meridian** (requires Organization table UPDATE)
  * [ ]  The Customer Access Request form dropdown shows **Central Meridian**, **Central Riverside**, **Central Crestline** — submitting the form still routes correctly (backend `Value` strings unchanged)
  * [ ]  No regressions in save/submit/navigation behavior
  * [ ]  `dotnet build` passes with 0 errors

---

## Out of Scope (Future Work)

* C# property names (e.g., `PEOHQControlNum`, `fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID`)

issues.title: feat(db): Add configurable permission flag columns to Organization_Security_Group
issues.description:
Currently, the `fnGetOneNListIDsUserHasPermissionsFor` and `BO_fnGetOneNListUserHasPermissionsFor` TVFs hardcode special access behaviors (Northline cross-access, Baymark cross-access, AllRegion contracting agency filter) by comparing against hardcoded group IDs or resolving groups by name. This makes it impossible for admins to assign these behaviors to new groups without a developer modifying SQL, and breaks silently when groups are renamed.

**Scope:** Add three nullable bit columns to `Organization_Security_Group` and seed initial values for the groups that currently have these behaviors hardcoded.

New columns:

| Column | Applies To | Behavior |
|--------|------------|----------|
| `HasNorthlineAccess` | PM / LIMITED groups | Group also sees all `IsNorthlinePurchase = 1` records org-wide |
| `HasCHSAccess` | PM / LIMITED groups | Group also sees all `IsCHSPurchase = 1` records org-wide |
| `HasAllACCAccess` | Region groups | Group sees all records where ContractingAgency LIKE `'%Region%'` |

Create a new migration file `Source/Migrations/YYYYMMDD_AddSecurityGroupPermissionFlags.sql`:

`ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Organization_Security_Group]
    ADD [HasNorthlineAccess]  bit NULL,
        [HasCHSAccess]    bit NULL,
        [HasAllACCAccess] bit NULL;
GO

-- Seed existing groups with flags that match current hardcoded behavior
UPDATE [dbo].[Organization_Security_Group] SET HasNorthlineAccess = 1 WHERE ID = 15;  -- Sequoia (PM TN)
UPDATE [dbo].[Organization_Security_Group] SET HasCHSAccess   = 1 WHERE ID = 16;  -- Halcyon
UPDATE [dbo].[Organization_Security_Group] SET HasNorthlineAccess = 1 WHERE ID = 69;  -- PL C2E (new — mirrors Sequoia)

-- Seed JPO Region group and Sandbox via name (last time names are used for this)
UPDATE g SET g.HasAllACCAccess = 1
FROM [dbo].[Organization_Security_Group] g
WHERE g.Name = 'JPO-Meridian SUPT CONTRACT OFF GROUP' AND g.fk_Organization_ID = 4;

UPDATE g SET g.HasAllACCAccess = 1
FROM [dbo].[Organization_Security_Group] g
WHERE g.Name = 'PO Region Owners' AND g.fk_Organization_ID = 3;
GO
`

**Acceptance Criteria:**

*  Migration runs without error on a clean local dev database
  * [ ]  `Organization_Security_Group` has three new nullable bit columns: `HasNorthlineAccess`, `HasCHSAccess`, `HasAllACCAccess`
  * [ ]  After migration, `SELECT ID, HasNorthlineAccess, HasCHSAccess, HasAllACCAccess FROM Organization_Security_Group WHERE ID IN (15, 16, 69)` returns: ID 15 → Northline=1, ID 16 → Baymark=1, ID 69 → Northline=1
  * [ ]  JPO-Meridian group has `HasAllACCAccess = 1`
  * [ ]  PO Region Owners group has `HasAllACCAccess = 1`
  * [ ]  All other existing groups have `NULL` for all three columns (no unintended data change)
  * [ ]  Migration is idempotent — running twice does not error or corrupt data

**Unit Test Requirements:**

* In `Source/OneNListApp.Tests/Service/`, add `SecurityGroupServiceTests.cs`
* Add a `TestBuilders.AValidSecurityGroup()` builder method returning an `Organization_Security_Group` with `HasNorthlineAccess = null`, `HasCHSAccess = null`, `HasAllACCAccess = null`
* Test cases (use `MockDbSetHelper.CreateMockDbSet` pattern from existing service tests):
  * `GetByOrganizationAsync_ReturnsGroups_WithFlagPropertiesAccessible` — seeds a group with `HasNorthlineAccess = true`, confirms the returned entity has the flag set
  * `GetByOrganizationAsync_WhenFlagsNull_ReturnsGroupWithNullFlags` — confirms null flags round-trip correctly
* No database required — use Moq + `MockDbSetHelper`

issues.title: refactor(sql): Replace hardcoded group IDs and name lookups in fnGetOneNListIDsUserHasPermissionsFor
issues.description:
The current function has two forms of fragility:

1. `fnResolveSecurityGroupId` resolves groups by `Name` — breaks when admins rename a group
2. `@WINT_securityGroupId = 15` and `@NETE_securityGroupId = 16` are hardcoded IDs — new groups can never get these behaviors

Replace all of this with reads from the new flag columns. Deliver as a new migration SQL file: `Source/Migrations/YYYYMMDD_Refactor_fnGetOneNListIDsUserHasPermissionsFor.sql`

**Changes inside the function body:**

**Remove** these declarations and their SET assignments:

* `@WINT_securityGroupId`, `@NETE_securityGroupId`
* `@JPO_ACC_securityGroupId` (was resolved by name)
* `@MiltechSandbox_ACC_securityGroupId` (was resolved by name)

**Add** flag variable declarations and populate them after the existing `@accessLevel`/`@securityGroupId` SELECT:

`DECLARE @hasNorthlineAccess bit, @hasCHSAccess bit, @hasAllACCAccess bit;
SELECT @hasNorthlineAccess  = HasNorthlineAccess,
       @hasCHSAccess    = HasCHSAccess,
       @hasAllACCAccess = HasAllACCAccess
FROM [dbo].[Organization_Security_Group]
WHERE ID = @securityGroupId;
`

**PM / LIMITED branch** — replace the nested `if @securityGroupId = @Sequoia` / `if @securityGroupId = @Halcyon` chain with three separate INSERT blocks:

`-- 1. Always insert own PM records
INSERT INTO @output
SELECT onen.ID FROM [dbo].[OneNList] onen
INNER JOIN [dbo].[LookupItem] lkp ON lkp.ID = onen.fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID
INNER JOIN [dbo].[LookupItem_PMPDExt] pmext ON pmext.fk_LookupItem_ID = lkp.ID
WHERE fk_OrganizationId = @organizationId
  AND pmext.fk_PMSecurityGroupID = @securityGroupId
  AND onen.PEOHQControlNum > 0
  AND fk_ActionStatus_Lookup_ID != @deletedRecordId;

-- 2. Northline cross-access (no org filter — matches original OR behavior)
IF @hasNorthlineAccess = 1
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO @output
    SELECT onen.ID FROM [dbo].[OneNList] onen
    WHERE onen.IsNorthlinePurchase = 1
      AND onen.ID NOT IN (SELECT onenID FROM @output);
END

-- 3. Baymark cross-access
IF @hasCHSAccess = 1
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO @output
    SELECT onen.ID FROM [dbo].[OneNList] onen
    WHERE onen.IsCHSPurchase = 1
      AND onen.ID NOT IN (SELECT onenID FROM @output);
END
`

**Region branch** — replace `if @securityGroupId = @JPO_ACC_securityGroupId` with `if @hasAllACCAccess = 1`. Keep `@C3T_ACC_securityGroupId = 4` and `@DataAnalytics_ACC_securityGroupId = 25` as hardcoded IDs (these never used name-based lookup and remain unchanged).

**Acceptance Criteria:**

*  Function compiles without error after migration
  * [ ]  `fnResolveSecurityGroupId` is no longer called from this function
  * [ ]  `@WINT_securityGroupId` and `@NETE_securityGroupId` declarations are removed
  * [ ]  Calling the function with a user in group ID 15 (Sequoia) returns the same set of IDs as before the refactor (own PM records + all Northline records)
  * [ ]  Calling the function with a user in group ID 16 (Halcyon) returns the same set of IDs as before (own PM records + all Baymark records)
  * [ ]  Calling the function with a user in group ID 69 (PL C2E) now returns Northline records (previously returned none)
  * [ ]  Renaming the JPO-Meridian group in `Organization_Security_Group` does NOT change the records returned for a JPO user
  * [ ]  A newly created PM group with `HasNorthlineAccess = 1` returns Northline records for its members
  * [ ]  A PM group with all flags NULL returns only its own PM records (no Northline, no Baymark)
  * [ ]  Region groups with `HasAllACCAccess = NULL` are unaffected (fall through to existing Vantage/Beacon logic)

**Unit / Integration Test Requirements:**

* Add `Source/OneNListApp.Tests/Service/SecurityGroupPermissionTests.cs`
* These tests verify application-level behavior that calls through the TVF. Use a real local dev database (per project convention: do not mock DB for SQL-backed tests)
* Test cases:
  * `GetPermissions_ForGroupWithNorthlineFlag_IncludesNorthlineRecords` — create a test PM group with `HasNorthlineAccess = 1`, seed a Northline action, confirm it appears in results
  * `GetPermissions_ForGroupWithNoFlags_ExcludesNorthlineRecords` — same setup but flag = NULL, confirm Northline action is absent
  * `GetPermissions_ForGroupWithCHSFlag_IncludesCHSRecords`
  * `GetPermissions_ForGroupWithAllACCFlag_IncludesAllACCAgencyRecords`
  * `GetPermissions_AfterGroupRename_ReturnsUnchangedResults` — rename group, re-query, confirm same result set

issues.title: refactor(sql): Replace hardcoded group lookups in BO_fnGetOneNListUserHasPermissionsFor
issues.description:
**Description:**

`BO_fnGetOneNListUserHasPermissionsFor` is used by BI report views (not the application directly). It has identical branching logic and the same name-based `fnResolveSecurityGroupId` calls as the main function. Apply the same flag-driven refactor so both functions stay in sync and BI reports are also unaffected by group renames.

Deliver as `Source/Migrations/YYYYMMDD_Refactor_BO_fnGetOneNListUserHasPermissionsFor.sql`.

The changes mirror Ticket 2 exactly — same flag variable declarations, same PM/LIMITED INSERT block split, same Region branch replacement — applied to the BO function body.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

*  Function compiles without error after migration
  * [ ]  `fnResolveSecurityGroupId` is no longer called from this function
  * [ ]  Row counts returned by BI report queries match pre-refactor counts for all organizations
  * [ ]  Renaming the JPO-Meridian group does NOT change BI report output
  * [ ]  A user in a group with `HasNorthlineAccess = 1` returns the same BI records as a Sequoia user did before the refactor

**Unit / Integration Test Requirements:**

* Add `BO_SecurityGroupPermissionTests.cs` in the same test class pattern as Ticket 2
* Test cases mirror Ticket 2 but call through the BO function:
  * `BO_GetPermissions_ForGroupWithNorthlineFlag_IncludesNorthlineRecords`
  * `BO_GetPermissions_ForGroupWithNoFlags_ExcludesNorthlineRecords`
  * `BO_GetPermissions_AfterGroupRename_ReturnsUnchangedResults`
* Additionally: add a parity test that calls both functions with the same user/org and asserts the returned ID sets are equal — catches future divergence

Show `#pmBehaviorFlags` when selected access level = 4 or 6; hide otherwise * Show `#accBehaviorFlags` when selected access level = 5; hide otherwise * On page load, apply the same show/hide based on issues.title: improvement: Prevent automatic re-authentication after user logout
